purpose: Verify AP receipt occupation in an older RR snapshot and the reversal progress projection.
data: One isolated migration-backed AP schema with one PO, receipt, detail and AP invoice. Each projection unit case uses one receipt and at most two details in memory.
concurrency: Two overlapping transactions in the AP correctness case. Projection cases are serial.
repetitions: One AP test and two projection tests, each discovered once per applicable workflow run.
thresholds: Current reads see a newly committed AP occupation and identify release. Projection preserves the PO and receipt statuses and rejects wrong-detail, missing-evidence and exceeded-quantity inputs.
trigger: Use the existing routine Node integration and unit discovery, with no new job, runner, trigger or capacity workload.
cost: The local AP fixture case took about four seconds including its private schema migrations. The two projection unit assertions take milliseconds. CI runner time and critical path are unmeasured.

cases: AP receipt invoice claims see the committed active line despite an earlier RR snapshot
